input.quote: 19.2 For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria. Hosted Services will conform throughout the subscription term. ... 19.4 For breach of Section 19.1 or 19.2, Vendor shall promptly re-perform, repair, or replace the nonconforming item at no charge. If Vendor cannot do so within a reasonable period, Customer may terminate the affected item and receive a refund of Fees paid for it.
input.rationale: Section 19 meets the checklist at or above the preferred level and is not swallowed by any disclaimer. 19.1 warrants professional and workmanlike performance by qualified personnel and material conformance of Services and Deliverables to documentation and specifications, with no time limit on the services warranty (better than the 90-day preferred / 30-day fallback floor). 19.2 gives Deliverables 90 days from the later of delivery or acceptance and warrants the hosted software (Services include hosted software per §1.8) will conform throughout the subscription term, which equals or exceeds the 12-month software position. 19.3 carries the compliance-with-Applicable-Law and no-malicious-code warranties, and 19.4 supplies repair/replacement/re-performance plus a refund of Fees paid, expressly non-exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims. 19.5 disclaims only implied warranties and states that no disclaimer limits an express warranty, so there is no "AS IS" gutting. Minor points short of the ideal, noted but not redlined: the malicious-code warranty is limited to code "intentionally introduced by Vendor", and the refund is available only after Vendor fails to cure within a reasonable period rather than at Customer's election.
